_comment: Mutations that put the AGPL-3.0 section 13 'the published source is the
running code' defect BACK into the branch, by breaking the ONE script
that makes the claim true.
THE DEFECT (measured 2026-11-07, review panel #5 on PR #64, and confirmed
by BOTH reviewers who answered): the container image is built from the
Docker build CONTEXT (the Dockerfile ends with `COPY . .`), while the
archive the offer publishes is the COMMITTED tree, and `git pull` never
removes untracked files. So a checkout with local changes produced a
running image containing files the published source did not contain -- and
the offer claimed they were the same code.
THE FIX is ops/scripts/record_deployed_commit.sh: it records the commit it
is about to build into .env, it REFUSES to stamp a checkout that is
not the committed tree, and it REFUSES to stamp a commit that was never
published. One implementation, shared by update.sh and the
MANUAL deploy sequence in AGENTS.md -- the manual path is the one the
operator actually uses, and a fix that only fires on the path nobody uses
is decorative (that was the SECOND half of the panel's finding).
THE SECOND DEFECT (measured 2026-11-09, review panel): the stamp took
`git rev-parse HEAD` with no check that the commit exists in the public
repository. The manual deploy path is `git pull origin main` with no
`git reset --hard`, so a local commit or a non-fast-forward merge leaves
HEAD unpushed -- and the offer points at
https://github.com/DiverseInc/DepthSight/archive/<commit>.tar.gz, which
is a 404 for a commit that was never pushed, while the page says the
commit is public. The script now asks `git branch -r --contains HEAD`
and refuses when no pushed ref contains the commit.
THE THIRD DEFECT (measured 2026-11-09, review panel, finding F1 raised by
3 of 6 engines): `git branch -r --contains HEAD` accepts a commit
contained by ANY remote-tracking branch of ANY remote -- origin/feature,
or a branch of a second remote -- and it reads the LOCAL remote-tracking
cache, which is stale by construction. It also never checked WHICH
repository `origin` points at, and it never asked the LIVE remote
anything. frontend/source.html says the running service is deployed from
the `main` branch of https://github.com/DiverseInc/DepthSight, and the
offer publishes the archive of the stamped commit there, so the stamp is
only true when all of the following hold:
(a) the commit is in the history of refs/remotes/origin/main -- that one
ref, not some other branch and not some other remote;
(b) `origin` IS that public repository (https and ssh forms, with or
without the trailing `.git`);
(c) the LIVE remote agrees: `git ls-remote origin main` has to answer,
it has to have a `main` branch, and the commit has to be an
ancestor of it -- a remote that cannot be reached is a REFUSAL,
never an assumption.
Mutants K to Q below put each of those three defects back, one at a time.
EVERY NEEDLE BELOW IS ASSERTED UNIQUE BEFORE USE: each occurs EXACTLY ONCE
in its file, measured against the file's bytes. A needle that matched two
sites would make the mutation meaningless, because the harness replaces
only the first hit; a needle that matched nothing would make the mutant
SKIP, and a SKIP is not a pass.
MUTANTS
A  the dirty-check refusal is removed, so a checkout with local changes
is stamped and the offer's claim becomes false. Killed by
test_an_untracked_file_is_refused and
test_a_modified_tracked_file_is_refused.
B  the missing-environment-file refusal is removed, so the script creates
a stub .env. That would start the application with NO configuration
at all -- a silent outage. Killed by
test_a_missing_environment_file_is_refused and
test_a_missing_environment_file_is_not_created.
C  the value is APPENDED instead of replaced, so .env ends up carrying
two DEPLOYED_COMMIT lines and the published commit is ambiguous.
Killed by test_an_existing_value_is_replaced_not_appended and
test_recording_twice_leaves_exactly_one_commit_line.
D  the carriage-return handling is dropped, so a Windows-edited .env has
its line endings rewritten. Killed by
test_a_crlf_environment_file_keeps_its_carriage_returns.
E  the project-root lookup is broken, so the script stamps the directory
it was started in instead of the project root. Killed by
test_run_from_a_subdirectory_it_still_stamps_the_root.
F  the refusal reports SUCCESS, so a dirty checkout is stamped anyway
and the deploy carries on. Killed by
test_an_untracked_file_is_refused.
G  the not-a-git-repository check is removed, so the script runs outside
a checkout and fails in a way that is not a clean refusal. Killed by
test_outside_a_git_repository_the_script_refuses.
H  the stamp is written to the wrong file, so the value never reaches the
.env the api service reads. Killed by
test_a_clean_checkout_records_the_commit.
I  the NOT-PUBLISHED refusal is removed, so a commit that was never
pushed is stamped and the offer publishes a 404 as the source.
Killed by test_a_commit_that_was_never_pushed_is_refused and
test_the_refusal_of_an_unpublished_commit_writes_nothing.
J  the published check asks about the PARENT commit instead of the
commit being deployed, so the commit that is actually stamped is
never the commit that was checked. Killed by
test_a_commit_that_was_never_pushed_is_refused (the pushed parent
passes the check, the unpushed child is stamped) and by
test_a_pushed_commit_is_stamped.
K  the 'origin IS the public repository' verdict is neutered, so a
PRIVATE FORK, another project or another host is accepted and the
stamp advertises an archive url that is a 404. Killed by
test_any_other_url_is_refused (nine other urls, each refused).
L  the 'there is no origin remote at all' refusal is removed, so a
checkout with no origin is carried on to the next check instead of
being told plainly that there is nothing to check against. Killed by
test_a_checkout_with_no_origin_remote_at_all_is_refused.
M  the 'is it on refs/remotes/origin/main' check is neutered, so a
commit that is NOT on the public main branch is stamped and the
page's promise about `main` becomes false. Killed by
test_a_commit_the_local_cache_has_not_caught_up_with_is_refused
(the live remote's main DOES contain the commit, the local copy of
origin/main does not, and the mutant stamps it anyway) and by
test_a_commit_published_on_another_branch_is_refused.
N  the 'does the LIVE remote's main contain the commit' check is
neutered, so a commit the remote no longer has is stamped. Killed
by test_a_remote_that_no_longer_has_the_commit_is_refused (the
remote's main was rewound and the mutant stamps it anyway) and by
test_the_refusal_of_a_stale_remote_writes_nothing.
O  the 'the live remote could not be asked' refusal is removed, so an
UNREACHABLE remote is treated as a remote with no main branch
instead of a hard refusal -- the script assumes rather than asks.
Killed by test_an_unreachable_remote_is_refused_loudly.
P  the 'not on the main branch' refusal reports SUCCESS, so the script
carries on and stamps a commit that is not on main. Killed by
test_a_commit_the_local_cache_has_not_caught_up_with_is_refused
and by test_a_commit_published_on_another_branch_is_refused.
Q  the 'origin is not the public repository' refusal reports SUCCESS,
so the script carries on and stamps a commit in a private fork.
Killed by test_any_other_url_is_refused and by
test_the_refusal_of_another_url_writes_nothing.
R  the deploy stamp stops recording the commit it is about to build, so
the running container can never know which build it is. THIS MUTANT
USED TO LIVE IN source_offer_deployed_commit.json AND IT SURVIVED
THERE (measured 2026-11-09). It was not a hole in the PRODUCT: it
was a MISFILED MUTANT. The pytest_target of that spec was four test
files, NONE of which is a test of this script, so no test in that
target could ever observe a defect injected here -- and the harness
reported a survivor for a FILING reason, which reads to a human
like a hole in the product. It is filed HERE, in the spec whose
target contains the tests that read this script's bytes. The needle
and the replace string are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the ones the survivor
was measured with. Killed by test_the_stamp_records_the_commit (in
tests/test_record_deployed_commit_script.py) and by the behavioural
tests in tests/test_deployed_commit_public_ref.py, which run the
REAL script and see an empty DEPLOYED_COMMIT.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/deployed_commit_script.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the dirty-check refusal is removed, so a checkout with local changes is stamped
B: the missing-environment-file refusal is removed, so the script creates a stub .env
C: the commit is appended instead of replaced, so .env carries two DEPLOYED_COMMIT lines
D: the carriage-return handling is dropped, so a Windows-edited .env loses its endings
E: the project-root lookup is broken, so the script stamps the directory it was started in
F: the refusal reports success, so a dirty checkout is stamped anyway
mutations.needle:
echo "  git checkout -- <path>   # discard ONE path's changes, deliberately" >&2
    exit 1
mutations.replace:
echo "  git checkout -- <path>   # discard ONE path's changes, deliberately" >&2
    exit 0

mutations.label: G: the not-a-git-repository check is removed, so the script runs outside a checkout
H: the stamp is written to the wrong file, so the value never reaches the api service
I: the not-published refusal is removed, so a commit that was never pushed is stamped
J: the published check asks about the parent commit, so the commit being stamped is never the one that was checked
K: the 'origin IS the public repository' verdict is neutered, so a fork or another host is accepted
L: the 'there is no origin remote at all' refusal is removed, so a checkout with no origin is carried on
M: the 'is it on refs/remotes/origin/main' check is neutered, so a commit that is not on the public main branch is stamped
N: the 'does the LIVE remote's main contain the commit' check is neutered, so a commit the remote no longer has is stamped
O: the 'the live remote could not be asked' refusal is removed, so an unreachable remote is assumed to be empty
mutations.needle: if ! REMOTE_MAIN_RAW=$(git ls-remote origin main 2>/dev/null); then

mutations.label: P: the 'not on the main branch' refusal reports success, so the script carries on and stamps a commit that is not on main
mutations.needle:
echo "  git push origin HEAD:main   # publish it on main, then deploy again" >&2
        echo "  git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main   # or deploy a published commit" >&2
        echo >&2
        echo "NOTHING HAS BEEN CHANGED OR DELETED BY THIS SCRIPT." >&2
        exit 1
mutations.replace:
echo "  git push origin HEAD:main   # publish it on main, then deploy again" >&2
        echo "  git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main   # or deploy a published commit" >&2
        echo >&2
        echo "NOTHING HAS BEEN CHANGED OR DELETED BY THIS SCRIPT." >&2
        exit 0

mutations.label: Q: the 'origin is not the public repository' refusal reports success, so the script carries on and stamps a commit in a fork

    echo >&2

mutations.replace:
